name: Three-Level Spot Stress
situation: 3rd & 4, +42, snapped at tempo before the nickel can re-communicate his apex assignment

summary.motive: Layer flat, spot/curl, and vertical takeoff off one shoulder so the apex nickel must defend three landmarks with two responsibilities, then beat the rotation clock with a one-hitch rhythm throw.
summary.whyItWorks: The spot sits precisely in the void between the flat and the deep drop-off — close enough that the nickel can't expand without surrendering the catch, far enough that sitting on it leaves the flat wide open — and tempo denies the rotation any chance to arrive.
summary.failureMode: A pattern-match quarters call where the apex defender carries the spot man-to-man and the flat is owned by a scraping safety or linebacker, erasing the conflict entirely.

beats.title: 1. Apex Stress at Tempo
beats.text: Kelly snaps this before the nickel can settle into his apex landmark — he's still aligning while the ball is in play. The formation gives nothing away pre-snap, so the nickel must solve the flat/curl conflict live.

beats.title: 2. Three Levels Off One Shoulder
beats.text: The left side builds vertically in three layers: RB swings flat low, H settles the spot at exactly five yards, X takes off behind it all. The nickel cannot occupy two of those landmarks at once.

beats.title: 3. The Nickel Freezes
beats.text: With eyes locked on the quarterback, the nickel is stuck between driving on H’s catcher-box spot and expanding to the RB flat. The QB sees the hesitation and delivers on the one-hitch rhythm before rotation can help.

beats.title: 4. Ball Out Before Rotation
beats.text: Both safeties stay pinned by the vertical threats and never break down on the spot in time. H turns the five-yard grab upfield into green grass because the entire second level is flowing away from the throw.

relations.tell: H freezes in a catcher-box spot at exactly five yards with the RB flat swinging under and X clearing over the top — every other receiver leaves the picture immediately.
